newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco mayor predicts stadium passage - paper.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco mayor predicts stadium passage - paper.

text.p: San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown predicted that voters would embrace a $100 million bond measure to help build a new football stadium, according to a published report Wednesday.
"I think the stadium passes," Brown said, according to the Examiner, San Francisco's afternoon newspaper. "I don't think people are warming to it. I think people are embracing it."
To help finance the stadium, San Francisco Board of Supervisors passed a resolution earlier this month placing up to a $100 million revenue bond measure on the June 3 ballot.

The proposed stadium and retail project is expected to cost $537 million, including $250 million to build a stadium for the National Football League's San Francisco 49ers, and $200 million for the entertainment and shopping complex.
